citations.review_text: اللعبه جميله لكن برمجياتها سيئه مواصفات جهازي فوق المطلوب بكثير ورغم ذلك ببعض المناطق فيه دروب فريم قوي وتنزل الفريمات الى 40 50  لكن لمن خليت كلشي ايبك مب الترا صار افضل بس برضو باقي دروب خفيف

I wanted to like this game, but it ended up being a huge disappointment. The biggest issue is how poorly optimized it is. Performance is rough, which makes it hard to stay immersed.

The horror also falls flat. Instead of being scary, the enemies look ridiculous there is nothing scary about a floating smile face coming towards me, and their animations are ridiculous and very low effort. Any tension the game tries to build disappears the moment you see anything that's meant to be taken seriously.

On top of that, the gameplay gets repetitive almost immediately. Most of the experience is just walking around and flipping switches over and over. There's very little variety, and it quickly becomes boring.

The Backrooms is a great concept for a horror game, but this feels like a missed opportunity. Unless the optimization, enemy design, animations, and gameplay are significantly improved, I can't recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe character movement as limited by very short stamina or poor mobility mechanics.

citations.review_text:
The only thing more shocking than the fact this game isn't free is the seemingly unlimited positive reviews it has from various real life NPCs. There seems to be a lot of people on steam who would be very entertained by the drying of wet paint. If you wish to run around a room pointlessly as characters with a pathetic lung capacity then this game is for you!

As an indie game, it exists. That's about it... There are far better multiplayer horror/thriller games out there. I mean much much much better.

The game seems like it could be a good time (especially with a friend) but it does one thing that I almost can't forgive. It may sound petty, but it matters to me and perhaps will to someone else. The inability to sprint for a decent stretch is ridiculous. Any normal human being  has better mobility than this. It's just plain frustrating to try to move faster, only to be slowed down to the sound of heavy breathing after about ten yards. As I said, It may sound silly, but for me it makes the game and exercise in frustration. Sadly, I am contemplating a refund.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay loop as repetitive, consisting mainly of walking through rooms and flipping switches.

citations.review_text: It's eh same game play loop, both me and my friend found it dull and unfun can't recommend :/.

[b]Rating:[/b] ★★☆☆☆


[h3][b]Positives:[/b][/h3]
› Online Co-Op.
› Endless (to a certain point).
› Has a story mode.

[h3][b]Negatives:[/b][/h3]
› Repetitive.
› Lack of gameplay.

[h3][b]Community Items:[/b][/h3]
› None.

[b]Do I recommend this game?[/b]
No. I thought it would've been more fun, but it really is just "walk around and get chased" simulator. I know it's meant to be a liminal space, but there really was absolutely nothing within the first 30 minutes of the game to keep me hooked.

I did not enjoy my time. Right off the bat, the enemies were annoying and buggy, the rooms felt repetitive and boring, and the puzzles made 0 logical sense. I do realize this is a friendslop game, but it is very basic for what it is. Content over quality in this instance.

This game mistakes repetition for horror. You're just mindlessly running through levels until some random entity clips through a wall. Then you restart and do the exact same thing all over again. It's not scary or interesting, it's just boring and repetitive.
Its pretty buggy, repetitive, and gets kinda boring quick.  I could play a more fun backrooms game on Roblox, and thats free, unlike this game.

game is SO good, i really love wasting my time figuring out USELESS puzzles with my friend just to see some garbage "entity" here and there. I LOVE going through mazes to flip some switches, because if my character doesnt have his "almond water" every 5 minutes, he will LITERALLY go ABSOLUTELY insane and die. this game is not atmospheric, not scary, no real depth to the levels, and just not really fun unless youre insanely high, on dmt, or just have autism. 0/10

I wanted to like this game, but it ended up being a huge disappointment. The biggest issue is how poorly optimized it is. Performance is rough, which makes it hard to stay immersed.

The horror also falls flat. Instead of being scary, the enemies look ridiculous there is nothing scary about a floating smile face coming towards me, and their animations are ridiculous and very low effort. Any tension the game tries to build disappears the moment you see anything that's meant to be taken seriously.

On top of that, the gameplay gets repetitive almost immediately. Most of the experience is just walking around and flipping switches over and over. There's very little variety, and it quickly becomes boring.

The Backrooms is a great concept for a horror game, but this feels like a missed opportunity. Unless the optimization, enemy design, animations, and gameplay are significantly improved, I can't recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance drops and frame rate issues requiring them to lower their graphics settings.

citations.review_text: This game is an absolute master piece, and they really deserve to be charging 20-30 USD instead of $10. Sadly, I had to play on either the lowest or the 2nd to lowest graphics settings to get my game to run smoothly.

This game is just 12 hours of busy work in a backrooms setting. I played through the whole game with one other person and was very disappointed. I was fairly excited when we started bu by the end, every new level was met with a groan followed by our brains going numb. The optimization should also be noted. I'm not playing on the most powerful of computers but I can run something like Elden Ring at a stable 60fps with pretty good graphics settings. For this game, I played on the lowest graphics settings and barely got above 20fps. I wish I could recommend this game as it could be a great concept but after finishing the game, I'm just left exhausted. The only thing that made me keep going was playing with friends as that adds a little bit of fun but I really cannot recommend this game at all.

This game is so janky the enemies are poorly balanced. What is the point of the mimic pretending to be one of your squad when they are just in their monster form 99% of the time?

I tried to like this game, I've heard a lot of good things about it, saw a lot of videos on yt about it. It was hyped a lot.

While the idea of backrooms is fun and you can do a lot of stuff with it, the levels are just not it.
They are too big, the drag out too much. Most of the time you don't know where to go. I played it with my friend and it was our first playthrough.

Enemies also aren't very interesting, the dogs just make a loud noise and barely work when you flash your light at them, animations are very choppy. Idea of doppelganger very fun, but made very poorly. We only heard one voiceline of him and straight to chase which usually ends with someone dead.

As it is right now, I can't recommend it. Scale down every level in like half and then you might have interesting time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe some levels as very short or consisting merely of running from one end of the map to the other.

citations.review_text: I've beaten the game two and a half times so far. It's very, very fun, but it definitely has problems. Sometimes items will fall through the map, and several of my friends have had frequent crashes, including myself once or twice. The proximity based voice chat is bugged as well, with it frequently breaking or transmitting practically every little noise out of your mic with no in-between. It also isn't the *most* polished either, with a good amount of fairly jank animations with no smoothing / tweening between them. Some maps are also very barebones as well, lasting either seconds at most (the air castle level) or are no more than just running to the other end of the map. To give some examples, there is the houses and hills level, where the only objective is to run from one end to the other while going inside when night falls. We even tried over several playthroughs to get the puppets that come out during the night to attack us by keeping the lights on, but nothing happened. They just sat outside. The worst one is probably the arcade, though, which is a long hallway where the only "puzzle" is finding a ticket on the opposite side of the room for the elevator code. Some levels are pretty fun, though. The dark maze with the LIDAR tool and the second set of Fun+ levels near the end for example are both very fun, along with most other levels in the game. I'd say 80% of the game is enjoyable. I'd definitely recommend it if you have a group of friends, but there are some caveats.
